body.p: Status
Claims 1-20 are pending and stand rejected. Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration of the application in view of the accompanying amendments and remarks. Rejections Under 35 U.S.C. § 103
Claims 1, 3-12 and 16-20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over US 5,921,422 ("Hunter"). Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and withdrawal of this rejection.
Claim ]

Without necessarily agreeing with the rejection, Applicant has amended claim 1 to make it clearer that the "clip portions" comprise curved (convex) surfaces that terminate at free edges that "are located closer to each other than respective portions of the respective curved surfaces immediately adjacent to the respective terminal free edges." Exemplary support for this amendment is found in Applicant's disclosure at Figure 3, and in the related written description. No new matter is added.

Hunter does not teach or suggest the claimed structure. Instead, Hunter teaches spring clips 106 that are inserted into stands 108, and configured to grip an enclosure (e.g., a computer housing) that is inserted into the stand. See, e.g., Hunter at col. 2, 11. 24-55. As shown in Figure 1, the ends of the spring clips 106 have proximal portions that curve inward towards each other, and distal portions that curve outward away from each other. The "terminal free edges" of Hunter's spring clips are located at the ends of the outwardly-curved portions, rather than being "located closer to each other than respective portions of the respective curved surfaces immediately adjacent to the respective terminal free edges," as recited in claim 1. Thus, Hunter does not anticipate claim 1.
It also would not have been obvious to modify Hunter to arrive at the structure of claim 1.
Hunter provides a system that is intended to facilitate efficient and effective assembly of the housing

to the stands, which is achieved by simply pushing the housing into the stands. See, e.g., Hunter at col. 1, 11. 56-60 ("Most important, the combination of spring clips and snap-on stands facilitate automatic manufacturing, enabling the enclosure to simply be pressed against the clips and stands."). The outward curves provided on Hunter's spring clips clearly are necessary to allow the spring clips to enter the openings 104 provided on opposite sides of the housing. For example, Figure 2 shows how the outward curves extend outward and upward to define a funnel-like entry to receive the incoming housing. The outward curves act like ramps to flex the spring slip outwards as the housing is inserted. Eliminating the outward curves would make it impossible to attach the housing to the stand, because the housing would push down on the spring clip ends and drive them towards each other, rather than away from each other.

Thus, it would not have been obvious to modify Hunter's spring clip to have "terminal free edges" that are "located closer to each other than respective portions of the respective curved surfaces immediately adjacent to the respective terminal free edges," as recited in claim 1, because the resulting structure would define ramp-like shapes that would drive the spring clip ends together as the housing is inserted. Such a modification would render Hunter unsatisfactory for its intended use, and there would be no reasonable expectation that the modification would yield a successful result.
For at least these reasons, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of claim 1 and all claims depending therefrom.

Claim 4 is amended to recite supports that extend from the plate to hold the plate at a spaced distance from an object to which the plate is secured. Exemplary support for this amendment is found in Applicant's Specification at page 9, line 29 to page 10, line 4. Examples of such supports are shown in broken lines in Figures 2 and 3. No new matter is added. The cited art does not teach or suggest this feature. Thus, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of claim
4 for this additional reason.

Claim 11 is amended to clarify that the "the grip portion extends from the respective convex side of the first clip portion at a location between and spaced from the respective first end and the respective terminal free end of the first clip portion." Exemplary support for this amendment is found in Applicant's Disclosure at Figure 3 and the related written description. No new matter is added. Hunter does not teach or suggest this structure. At most, Hunter shows outward bends of the spring clip that extend continuously from the surface defining the concave portions. These outward bends do not extend from a convex surface, and do not extend at a location between and spaced from "the respective first end and the respective terminal free end of the first clip portion." Thus, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of claim 11 and all claims depending therefrom for this additional reason.

Claim 10 is amended to depend from claim 11, and recite "wherein the respective curved surface of the first clip portion extends parallel to the main plane through a first distance, the grip portion extends parallel to the main plane from a first end to a second end through a second distance, and the second distance is less than the first distance." An example of this structure is shown in Figure 3 of Applicant's disclosure. No new matter is added. Hunter also does not teach or suggest this structure. At most, Hunter teaches outward bending portions of the spring clip that are the same length as the remainder of the spring clip. Thus, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of claim 10 for this additional reason.

Claim 17 is amended to clarify that "the respective terminal free edge of each clip portion is located at a greater distance from the main plane than any other part of the respective clip portion." An example of this structure is shown in Figure 3 of Applicant's disclosure. No new matter is added. Hunter also does not teach or suggest this structure. Rather, the terminal free edges of Hunter's spring clips are located at the ends of the outwardly-bent portion. Thus, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of claim 17 for this additional reason.

Claims 2 and 13-15 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Hunter in view of US 8,662,455 ("Hernandez"). Hernandez is cited only to teach certain material selections, and does not cure the deficiencies of the rejection of claim 1. Thus, Applicant respectfully requests reconsideration and allowance of claims 2 and 13-15 for the same reasons as stated above. Conclusion
No new matter is added in this response. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests

reconsideration of the application in view of the attached amendments and remarks. The Examiner is encouraged to telephone the undersigned attorney of record to discuss any outstanding issue that prevents allowance at this time.
Respectfully submitted, /Michael P.F. Phelps/
